extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on F1000Research's open, post-publication peer review process: expectations for selecting reviewers, how peer review reports and approval statuses are defined, the editorial team's role, and how to revise and respond to reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open identity transparency (NISO standard)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F1000Research uses the NISO standard terminology: reviewer interacts with editor, other reviewers, authors; review information published (review reports, submitted manuscript, reviewer identities); post-publication commenting is open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-led reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review process for F1000Research is led by the authors, who are responsible for identifying appropriate experts from relevant fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before an article can be published, authors must suggest at least 5 reviewers who meet F1000Research reviewer criteria. The editorial team may also suggest suitable reviewers where required. Authors should not approach reviewers about the peer review process independently, as this has the potential to influence and invalidate their review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of suggested reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must suggest at least 5 reviewers before an article can be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested reviewers should meet the journal's reviewer criteria (see Finding Article Reviewers page). The editorial team may add suggestions to ensure balance and facilitate the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise for statistical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: If the study includes complex statistical analysis or new statistical methods, ensure at least one suggested reviewer has a proven track record as a statistics expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware the journal may ask you to suggest additional statistics experts as the peer review process progresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial team responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial team supports authors and manages aspects of the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their tasks include ensuring the reviewer criteria are met; acting as intermediary between authors and reviewers; contacting reviewers; ensuring all aspects of an article are reviewed; and checking the peer review reports before they are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published peer review reports and reviewer identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review reports are published alongside the article with the names and affiliations of the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This transparent publication of reports allows discussion of strengths and weaknesses and shows exactly what issues reviewers identified. All versions of the article and all peer review reports will remain published so anyone may see the history of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status: Approved
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved: No or only minor changes are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For original research, this means the aims and research methods are adequate; results are presented accurately; and the conclusions are justified and supported by the presented data or supporting material. Reviewers may suggest small changes to improve the article or correct minor errors, but these changes will not affect the peer review status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status: Approved with Reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved with Reservations: The reviewer believes the article has academic merit, but has asked for a number of small changes to the article, or specific, sometimes more significant revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should make clear that the changes requested are necessary for an Approved status to be awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status: Not Approved
rubrics_metrics.description: Not Approved: The article in its current form has issues that seriously undermine the findings and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crucial substantial revisions will be required for the paper to pass peer review. Not Approved is not a rejection — it is possible to improve an article’s status from Not Approved to Approved upon publication of a new version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient review threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: An article is considered to have been sufficiently reviewed when it has received two peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will be encouraged to revise and respond after receiving two peer review reports if the article has not yet passed peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for passing peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: An article is considered to have passed peer review when at least two 'Approved' statuses, or one 'Approved' and two 'Approved with Reservations' have been awarded by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some articles may have more than two peer review reports, for example when more than two reviewers accepted the invitation or when special expertise is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to revise and provide point-by-point responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should provide a direct point-by-point response to each reviewer when they submit the revised article version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response should explain how each reviewer’s comments have been addressed in the revisions; this assists original reviewers in re-reviewing and signals to other potential reviewers that feedback is being taken into consideration, making further reviews more likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-invitation of original reviewers after revision
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new version is published the original reviewers are re-invited to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can publish an updated report taking the revisions into account. Reviewers are especially encouraged to re-review if they had originally given an 'Approved with Reservations' or 'Not Approved' status, as they are asked to assess whether the work has been sufficiently improved to achieve a better approval status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review is part of an open, post-publication model
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review of articles on F1000Research takes place after publication under an open and transparent peer review model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model enables publication first and formal open peer review after; review reports, reviewer identities and the submitted manuscript are published to encourage transparent discussion.
